samples: This program models a traffic light as a small state machine. Given a current light and an event (timer expiry, emergency declared, or emergency cleared), it works out the next light: normal cycling goes red, green, yellow, red, an emergency forces flashing red, and clearing it returns to red. It can also replay a list of events and report each resulting light, and its `main` prints a short demo sequence with one emergency in the middle, needing only console access and nothing else (no network or files).

This program models a traffic light as a state machine: a pure function takes the current light (red, green, yellow, or flashing red) and an event (timer expiry, emergency declared, or emergency cleared) and returns the next light. Timers move it through the normal red, green, yellow cycle, an emergency forces flashing red that ignores timers, and clearing the emergency returns it to red. It also offers a function that applies a list of events in order and returns the resulting lights, plus a demo `main` that prints one such sequence to the console, so it is a small, self-contained, well-documented building block, with no network or file access, that you could reuse for simulation or testing.

This program models a traffic light as a state machine. It cycles Red, Green, Yellow, Red on timer events, switches to flashing red when an emergency is declared (the light stays flashing through timer events), and returns to Red when the emergency is cleared. It offers a function that computes the next light, a function that returns every light shown for a list of events, and a demo entry point that prints a short sequence with an emergency in the middle. It is pure logic apart from console printing, with built-in examples documenting the expected transitions, so it is easy to reuse as a small, self-contained building block.

This program models a traffic light as a state machine. It cycles Red, Green, Yellow, Red on timer events, jumps to a flashing red when an emergency is declared (staying there through timer ticks), and returns to Red when the emergency is cleared. It can also replay a list of events from a starting light to get the sequence of lights shown. Its runnable entry point only prints the results of a built-in demo sequence with one emergency, so it's best used as a reusable state-transition library or a teaching example rather than as a configurable tool.

This program models a traffic light as a state machine: given the current colour and an event (timer expiring, emergency declared, or emergency cleared), it returns the next colour. It cycles red, green, yellow, red on timer events, switches to flashing red on an emergency (staying there until the emergency is cleared, which returns it to red), and can also apply a whole list of events to report each resulting colour. It is pure, testable logic with documented examples, and its demo entry point simply prints the colours for one fixed sequence, so it is a small reference or building block rather than a configurable tool.
